questions.q: What does Query Store persist that DMVs like sys.dm_exec_query_stats do not survive?
options: Nothing -- Query Store and sys.dm_exec_query_stats store the exact same information
Backup file locations
Query text, every plan a query has used, and runtime statistics per plan, persisted to disk across service restarts
Only the current execution plan, discarded on the next query run
questions.explain: This persistence across restarts is exactly what lets Query Store answer 'was this always slow, or did something change.'

questions.q: Is Query Store on by default on Azure SQL Database, or does it need to be turned on?
options: It must always be turned on manually, on every platform, with no default
It can only be enabled by Microsoft support
It is never available on Azure SQL Database
It is on by default on Azure SQL Database; on SQL Server on-prem or a VM, it's turned on per database with ALTER DATABASE
questions.explain: This platform difference is worth knowing directly -- Azure SQL Database defaults it on.

questions.q: In a query's Plan Summary view, what does seeing two separate clusters of dots at very different average-duration heights usually mean?
options: The query ran under two meaningfully different execution plans during those time periods
The database was in single-user mode during that period
Query Store has stopped recording data
The query returned different columns each time it ran
questions.explain: Each dot color/plan id in the legend corresponds to a distinct plan -- a height jump between clusters is a visible plan change.

questions.q: What does the Top Resource Consumers report let you do?
options: Show only queries written by a specific login
Delete queries that use too many resources
Automatically rewrite the worst-performing queries
Rank the top queries on a database by a chosen metric (duration, CPU time, logical reads, etc.) over a time window, instead of guessing which query to tune first
questions.explain: Selecting a bar in the report drills into that specific query's own Plan Summary view and text.

options: Forces Query Store to capture every single query with no filtering at all
Disables Query Store entirely
Skips capturing one-off ad hoc queries that ran once and never again, reducing noise in Query Store
Automatically forces the best plan for every query
questions.explain: Capturing only 'relevant' recurring queries keeps the store from filling with one-time noise.
